dialogues.speaker: Frejus
dialogues.text: So, how are the experiments going?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Phew... Glad to hear it.

choices.text: Do even geniuses worry about their experiments?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Haha, it sure would be nice if I really were a genius. To be honest, I'm just an ordinary fellow who's lived an ordinary life for thirty years. There's nothing special about me.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: I would have been more enthusiastic just a few years ago, but I was shot while rescuing hostages, and as a result, I often wake up in pain at night, so I ended up like this.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Gunshot wounds tend to be very troublesome like that. Fortunately, all the hostages were saved — that was one of the few highlights of my life.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why does Chenee call you a genius, then?

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Oh, uh, about that... I took her and the other newbies out for a party when she first joined... and I might have bragged about my abilities too much while drunk.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: All that "rejected the Institute three times" business... It was I, in truth, who was rejected. I'm no genius, just a normal person who dabbles in little gadgets.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: I didn't expect them to all believe me, and since our patrol work isn't all that interesting, they always pester me with questions when they get bored.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: As such, I've been forced to continue this charade... That said, while my work is nothing compared to the Institute's advanced research, I have constructed quite a few small, useful inventions.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Of course, I make them out of pocket, but I keep those greenhorns in the dark by saying that they're funded by the higher-ups, which makes them sound more cool. Please keep my secret, if you don't mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This will fall through one day, I know.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Yes, I'm aware. But I imagine their curiosity is limited, and in fact, many people have lost interest — only Chenee remains.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: Once she too gets bored, I shan't have to continue.

response.speaker: Frejus
response.text: I'm sure it'll make me feel a little better... and a little disappointed all at once. Such is base humanity, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Chenee
dialogues.text: What do you think of Frejus's remote cannon?

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Good, that's good.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You don't sound so excited...

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Ah... Sorry. I mean, it's not that I don't like it. It's just that I knew what the device would look like the moment I looked upon the blueprints.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Frejus is the one doing the hard work, and it does look hard. I see that he looks nervous, even though this is no big deal — there's no great risk of an accident occurring.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: "Playing the part of a genius" is pretty tiring, don't you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you getting at?

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: That he isn't a real genius. If I had to guess, he's just an ordinary person with a more active mind and ideas than usual.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: It was drunk boasting, you know, that whole "rejecting the Fontaine Research Institute's offer three times" business. He's been putting in the work to protect that lie since.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Ah, right. Please keep this a secret for me. Reckon he doesn't think I've noticed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And how did you find out?

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Probably because I really have rejected them myself, I guess? I'm somewhat aware of their standards. As for Frejus... He's a decent ways off from making the cut.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you're playing along with his act, then?

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: You could say so. Specifically, I play the role of the ignorant newcomer, asking him all manner of questions.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: And sometimes I will ask him something particularly difficult on purpose and look at him expectantly, at which he will try his best to hide his embarrassment.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: Then, I "accidentally" give him hints, and he will turn about and cough, pretending that he knew all along—

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: This whole process is quite fun, which is why I do not intend to expose him. Seeing him run around being busy is one of my favorite hobbies these days.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like this show will go on, then.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: I imagine it will — for a long time, in fact.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: As long as I don't tell him, he won't be able to tell. He even thinks that the newcomers' party was the first time we met, but it was a long time before that.

response.speaker: Chenee
response.text: He's so very inobservant. I'm sure he doesn't remember — or perhaps he doesn't care — who he blocked the bullet for that day.

choices.text: It's a rather novel experience, alright.
